title: Austin: Paving Progress, Special Recognition
summary:
*   City officials passed a unique resolution recognizing Miss Lole McSween for her extensive charity work and congratulating her on her upcoming marriage.
*   Major infrastructure initiatives were launched, including adopting paving specifications and ordering new paving for key streets like North Congress Avenue, West 6th Street, Lavaaca Street, and University Avenue.
*   The council began the process to close and vacate a 48.5-foot strip of land located north of Wooldridge School.

318
. Regular meeting of the City Council: Austin, Texas, Sept 12th 1912.
The Council was called to order by the Mayor: Roll called: Present Mayor Wooldridge,
Councilmen Haynes & Powell 3 Absent excused Councilmen Bartholomew & Hart 2 The minutes of
the last regular and subsequent recessed meetings were read and adopted.

. Petitions ,etc:

Fine Wm Powell The Mayor laid before the Council a petition from W M Powell, asking the
Council to remit a fine assessed against Willie Powell in the Recorders Court, which was
read and the petition granted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Haynes & Powell 3 Absent excused Councilmen Bartholomew & Hart 2 Building permits The
Mayor laid before the Council petitions from Yates & Cornwell, Yates & Cornwell W L
Hamilton & W L Parsley, asking for permission to erect certain W L Hamilton buildings
within the Fire limits, which were read ordered filed.
W L Parsley Unfinished business:
The Mayor laid before the Council a resolution appropriating the sum of $ 1,340.97 ,to pay
the claim of J W Maxwell for commissions collecting delinquent taxes, which was passed by
the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen Haynes & Powell 3
Absent Councilmen Bartholomew & Hart 2

New Business:
Mayor Wooldridge offered the following resolution:

Resolution on Miss Lole Mc Sween, an Austin girl, today marries Mr Scott McGuire, a
marriage of Kentucky gentleman, and after today Mrs McGuirewill probably cease to
Miss McSween live among us.
Miss McSween inspired by the Council and example of her good mother, Mrs C H Wilcox, whose
life for many years in Austin has been largely devoted to deeds of unpaid love and
charity, has herself like her noble mother gone in and out amongst the poor ,the ignorant,
the afflicted, the sorrowing and even the vicious of our people, unselfishly minister, to
their needs ,loved and respected for her life and appreciated for her unselfish
philanthropy.
Resolved, therefore, by the City Council of the City of Austin: That the Council
congratulates Miss McSween upon her impending happy marriage, and wishes for her in her
new abode a continued life of unselfishness and love, and wishes that when she is married
,such domestic felicity will be added to the happiness she has so largely gotten and has
so richly deserved from her public service.
Resolved that this resolution be entered upon the minutes of the City Council and a copy
thereof, oved the seal of the City, be transmitted with the compliments of the City
Council to Miss McSween.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Haynes & Powell 3
Absent Councilmen Bartholomew & Hart 2
